doc.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000

title: Audition at Dizzy's house with Parker, Powell and Roach
summary: Brown plays for Gillespie, Parker, Bud Powell and Max Roach, is hired, and tells his mother; he discusses their experience and his limited knowledge of bebop.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: we go back up to where we were, and I go to Dizzy Gillespie’s house the next day and there’s four guys there. Dizzy Gillespie, Charlie Parker, Bud Powell and Max Roach. Charlie Parker I had seen with Jay McShann. Bud Powell I had seen with Cootie Williams’ band. Max Roach I had seen in the theater with Benny Carter, and Dizzy I had seen with Cab. So I had seen all these people and I had heard them on record, but this was the first time. And then they started to play, it scared me to death. I mean I never heard anything like this before. But they played real fast. And that’s something I could do. So I guess maybe that’s why they kept me. But anyway he said, “Okay you’ll do.” We are going to work and he told me when. And I go back up to my aunt’s the next day and I called my mother. She said, “Which one of the bands did you take?” I said, “Uh, I didn’t take any of those?” She said, “Well what did you do?” I said, “I’m with Dizzy Gillespie.” She said, “Who?”
Those guys weren’t all that much older than you, were they? Mid-twenties perhaps?

But they were older than me in experience. That’s what counts. Not how old you are. They had experience. All these guys had been through the big bands and now they were in small groups playing like man you just wouldn’t believe how they played.
Were you that familiar with bebop up to that point?
No, the only bebop we had records of was Billy Eckstine when he was doing the big band stuff.
